questions.enonce_markdown:
Carefully examine the resurrection appearances.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** In the Fourth Gospel the resurrection stories are found in chapters 20 and 21. They include the discovery of the empty tomb and four appearances of the risen Jesus, and they show who saw him, what he said and what the appearances meant. (The other Gospels and 1 Corinthians 15:5-8 give further appearances, which are mentioned briefly below.)

**1. The empty tomb (20:1-10).** Mary Magdalene finds the stone removed and tells Peter and the beloved disciple. They run to the tomb and find the linen wrappings lying there. The beloved disciple "saw and believed", though they did not yet understand the scripture that he must rise.

**2. The appearance to Mary Magdalene (20:11-18).** Mary stays weeping at the tomb and sees two angels and then Jesus, whom she takes to be the gardener. She recognises him when he says her name, "Mary". He tells her not to hold on to him, because he has not yet ascended to the Father, and sends her to tell the disciples that he is ascending "to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God". She announces, "I have seen the Lord."

**3. The appearance to the disciples (20:19-23).** On the evening of the first day, the disciples are behind locked doors for fear of the Jewish authorities. Jesus comes and stands among them, says "Peace be with you", and shows his hands and side. They rejoice. He sends them as the Father has sent him, breathes on them, says "Receive the Holy Spirit" and gives them authority regarding the forgiveness of sins.

**4. The appearance to Thomas (20:24-29).** Thomas, who was absent, says that he will not believe unless he sees and touches the marks of the nails. A week later Jesus appears again, invites him to touch, and Thomas confesses, "My Lord and my God!" Jesus says, "Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe." This addresses later generations of believers.

**5. The appearance by the Sea of Tiberias (21:1-14).** Seven disciples have fished all night without success. A figure on the shore tells them to cast the net on the right side, and they catch a large number of fish. The beloved disciple says, "It is the Lord!" Jesus prepares breakfast and gives them bread and fish. The reference to a meal underlines that the risen Jesus is truly present.

**6. Jesus and Peter (21:15-19).** Jesus asks Peter three times whether he loves him and tells him to feed his lambs and tend his sheep. This restores Peter after his threefold denial and commissions him as shepherd.

**Meaning of the appearances.** They show that the risen Jesus is the same Jesus who was crucified, yet he is not limited as before: he enters closed rooms. They produce faith, bring joy and peace, restore failed disciples, give a commission and promise the Spirit. John's purpose is stated at 20:30-31: these things are written "so that you may come to believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and that through believing you may have life in his name".

**Conclusion.** The appearances in John are varied in setting and person, but they have common themes: recognition, faith, peace, mission and the continuing presence of Jesus with his followers.
